subject: Purchasing readiness: channel preference & AP constraints for CloudRidge
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cloudridgeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Purchasing readiness: channel preference & AP constraints for CloudRidge

Hi Elena — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the procurement side so we can keep the momentum going: 

1) Commercial path options we discussed:
   - Direct invoice / PO (CloudRidge issues PO to Redwood; monthly invoicing)
   - Corporate card (single monthly charge or card on file for pilot)
   - Cloud marketplace procurement (Azure Marketplace listing; want to confirm interest)

2) AP constraints you mentioned:
   - Standard 45–60 day net terms for enterprise vendors
   - Vendor onboarding requires vendor setup form + W-9 + SOC 2 evidence
   - Purchasing team prefers POs for anything > $50k ARR; occasional card exceptions for pilots

3) What we can provide now:
   - Draft SOW + MSA excerpt for legal review (attached SOW-CloudRidge-20261012-draft.pdf)
   - Formal quote spreadsheet with list pricing and pilot discounts (attached Redwood-quote-CloudRidge-20261012.xlsx)
   - SOC2 summary and attestation link (I’ve pasted the Drive link below)

Proposed next steps: 
- Can you confirm whether your procurement prefers PO or card for a 3‑month pilot? If PO, what is the contact and expected PO lead time?
- If you want to evaluate marketplace, I can loop in our partnerships lead to discuss listing timing and billing flow.
- I’ll follow up with Marissa (CS lead) to prepare a compact onboarding checklist to satisfy vendor setup quickly.

If helpful I can loop in Karthik from commercial ops to answer card-limit and billing questions — copying him here. Thanks,

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0186

Attachments: SOW-CloudRidge-20261012-draft.pdf (application/pdf), Redwood-quote-CloudRidge-20261012.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

References:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4821
- SOC2 folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2c3Example

From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cloudridgeanalytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudridgeanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Purchasing readiness: channel preference & AP constraints for CloudRidge

Thanks, Mina — really useful recap. A few clarifications from procurement side: 

- For pilots under $25k we usually accept a corporate card; anything expected to exceed that typically needs a PO. The pilot you outlined sounds like it may be ~$18k committed spend, so card would be fine from a policy standpoint.
- That said, our vendor onboarding team requires the W-9 + vendor questionnaire before we can put any vendor on file; PO creation waits for vendor setup to complete (usually 5–7 business days once we have docs).
- Marketplace billing is attractive (less internal paperwork) but finance will want to confirm tax handling (we’re on Azure Gov tenancy for some projects, so marketplace availability is a gating question).

Action items from our side:
- I’ll push your SOW and quote to procurement and request expedited vendor setup (procurement@cloudridgeanalytics.com).
- I can provide a single-use corporate card for the pilot if Redwood can invoice monthly and keep charges under the pilot cap.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept card for the initial pilot and transition to PO if we expand? Also please confirm which vendor docs you need up front so I can share them in one bundle.

Best,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudRidge Analytics
elena.ortiz@cloudridgeanalytics.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cloudridgeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Purchasing readiness: channel preference & AP constraints for CloudRidge

Elena — looping in with operational details and a recommended path: 

Short answer: yes, we can accept a corporate card for the pilot and transition to PO for longer commitments. A few notes: 

- Card workflow: we can process charges on a card-on-file monthly. We need the cardholder name, last 4, and billing email; we will send an online billing link for card submission (PCI-compliant).
- PO workflow: For PO invoicing we need vendor setup completed (W-9 or tax form, remit address) + a PO number to include on invoices. Billing cycles supported: monthly or net-30.
- Marketplace: If you want marketplace billing, we’ll need to confirm your subscription entitlement in Azure Gov; that will add ~2–3 weeks for listing and procurement validation.

To accelerate vendor setup I’ve attached a short vendor checklist we typically send to procurement. If procurement is ready to accept the attachments in one email, we can move the vendor setup to day 0 and produce a PO-ready invoice within 5 business days.

Next steps from Redwood ops:
- I’ll send the vendor checklist to procurement (one-offs: W-9, company legal name, remit address, SOC2 link).
- Mina/Marissa to confirm pilot start date and whether charges will stay below the $25k pilot cap.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: vendor-onboard-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cloudridgeanalytics.com>, procurement@cloudridgeanalytics.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Purchasing readiness: channel preference & AP constraints for CloudRidge

Thanks Elena — perfect. Quick confirm and proposed timeline: 

- Pilot billing method: corporate card for initial 90-day pilot (target spend ~$18k). Elena, if you can share the cardholder email or push the billing invite, we’ll get the test charge started the first week after kickoff.
- Vendor docs: procurement, please find the SOW + quote + vendor checklist attached; we’d appreciate vendor setup kick-off today so PO is possible if the pilot expands.
- Marketplace: we’ll hold on marketplace listing for now; if you want us to pursue Azure Gov compatibility we can kick off separately (estimate 2–3 weeks).

Proposed short timeline:
- Today: procurement acknowledges vendor docs and confirms card route.
- Within 2 business days: Redwood sends billing link for card-on-file + onboarding checklist to CloudRidge technical contact (Marissa will own onboarding).
- Week +2: pilot kickoff once card is validated and initial config completes.

Elena — are you able to confirm procurement@cloudridgeanalytics.com received the attachments and whether they want the vendor questionnaire in-line or as a secure form? If so I’ll mark the HubSpot deal RDW-4821 as "Ready for Procurement".

Thanks — excited to get this running.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0186

Attachments: Redwood-quote-CloudRidge-20261012.xlsx, SOW-CloudRidge-20261012-draft.pdf, vendor-onboard-checklist.pdf
